conclusion: The MoE pricing path is NOT generically divergent: 30B-A3B-TP2 agrees across runtimes at s=1 (1.000), s=2 (1.001) and s=4 (0.828 -- source OPTIMISTIC by 17%), and its ITL agrees to within 6%.

The divergence is SPECIFIC to 235B-TP8 and appears only ABOVE that arm's knee: s=1 agrees to 1% (388.1 vs 392.7), s=2 diverges 0.73x, s=4 diverges 14.65x (20,530.9 source vs 1,401.7 wheel = the ledgered simulation/results/235b value, reproduced exactly here).
The wheel run reproduces the ledgered 1,401.7 ms exactly, so the cross-check apparatus is faithful and the ledgered number stands.

EVERY arm's knee in this sweep is ITL-BOUND (binding='itl'), and ITL agrees across runtimes within 6-14% at every point measured, including 235B-TP8 s=4 (275.4 vs 318.5). The knee locations are therefore governed by the quantity the two runtimes agree on.

CONSEQUENCE: the MoE-arm knees stand. The caveat that must be written is narrower than feared -- the 235B-TP8 SATURATED-SIDE TTFT curve above its knee (s>=2) is runtime-dependent and must not be quoted as a measurement; its knee (s=1.12) and its s=1 row are runtime-robust.

kv_budgets_source_build.note: the wheel runtime (1.2.1) does not emit total_kv_blocks at RUST_LOG=warn, so a direct KV-budget diff was not obtainable; the behavioural evidence above localises the divergence to prefill admission on the one arm whose KV budget is smallest.
